report.summary: Chunk 3 of 6 of clones.py: helper functions for abstract tokens, fingerprint, token bag; CloneMemo class; start of unit_clusters.
risks: CloneMemo.__init__ | medium | _spec_by_lang parameter typed as dict but expected to map language strings to LanguageSpec; caller must ensure correct type. | Add type annotation or runtime check.

CloneMemo.exact_fp | low | Uses id(u) as key; if u is garbage-collected and id reused, cache could return stale value. Scope memo to one build_index call mitigates. | Ensure memo lifetime matches unit list lifetime.
unit_clusters | medium | Function signature includes memo parameter but body not shown; if memo is None, exact_fp may be recomputed. | Ensure memo is passed when available.
todos: Verify that _spec_by_lang is correctly typed and used.

handoff.purpose: Define abstract token helpers, fingerprint, token bag, and CloneMemo cache; start unit_clusters.

symbols.name: _abstract_tokens
symbols.note: Returns abstracted token list; uses python-specific or generic abstraction.

symbols.name: abstract_normalize
symbols.note: Returns space-joined abstract tokens for Type-2 matching.

symbols.name: _fingerprint_of_tokens
symbols.note: Returns first 12 hex chars of SHA-1 of joined abstract tokens.

symbols.name: token_bag
symbols.note: Returns Counter of abstract tokens for Type-3 near-miss.

symbols.name: CloneMemo
symbols.note: Caches exact and abstract fingerprints per unit.

symbols.name: CloneMemo.exact_fp
symbols.note: Returns exact fingerprint, computing and caching if needed.

symbols.name: CloneMemo.abstract_fp
symbols.note: Returns abstract fingerprint, computing and caching if needed.

symbols.name: CloneMemo.put_abstract_fp
symbols.note: Stores precomputed abstract fingerprint if not already cached.

claims.text: Two renamed-but-otherwise-identical units share this string exactly (the Type-2 signal).
claims.why: The function returns abstract tokens where identifiers become 'ID', numbers 'NUM', strings 'STR', keywords kept; thus renamed identifiers yield same string.

claims.text: The Type-2 fingerprint, computed from an ALREADY-abstracted token list. Exists so a caller that needs both the token bag and the fingerprint for the same unit can abstract once and derive both, instead of tokenizing the same string twice (see near_clusters).
claims.why: Function takes token list (already abstracted) and returns fingerprint; comment explains rationale.

claims.text: abstract_fingerprint delegates here so there is exactly ONE definition of the fingerprint -- deriving it in two places would let the near-miss pass and the renamed pass silently disagree about what a Type-2 match is.
claims.why: Both abstract_fingerprint and token_bag call _abstract_tokens; fingerprint is derived via _fingerprint_of_tokens, single definition.

claims.text: Multiset of ABSTRACTED tokens — the SourcererCC bag used for near-miss (Type-3) overlap. Abstracted (not raw) so a near-copy with renamed locals still overlaps heavily.
Per-unit derived fingerprints, computed once and shared by all three clone passes.
claims.why: Class caches exact and abstract fingerprints, used by unit_clusters, renamed_clusters, near_clusters (mentioned).

claims.text: WHY: the passes are independent functions over the SAME unit list, and each re-derived what a previous one had already computed. unit_clusters computes the exact fingerprint; renamed_clusters computed that exact fingerprint AGAIN (it needs it to exclude pure Type-1 clusters) plus the abstract one; near_clusters then derived the abstract one a third time. Normalization and abstraction are the two most expensive operations in the scan, so this was the dominant redundancy.
claims.why: The behavior of unit_clusters, renamed_clusters, near_clusters is not in this chunk; cannot verify.

claims.text: ONLY the two 12-char fingerprints are cached, never the token lists. The lists are the memory-heavy part -- all_units already retains full source text at ~22.5x source bytes -- and they are needed only *within* near_clusters, which derives its bag and its fingerprint from a single tokenization.
claims.why: Token lists not shown; all_units and near_clusters not in chunk; memory claim cannot be verified.

claims.text: Each entry holds a reference to its unit alongside the value, so an id() key can never be recycled onto a different object while the memo is alive.
claims.why: Cache stores tuple (u, value) where u is the unit object; id(u) used as key; reference prevents recycling.

claims.text: Scope one memo to one build_index call and drop it after: a module-level cache would leak across scans.
claims.why: build_index not in chunk; cannot verify scoping.

claims.text: Donate a fingerprint derived from tokens the caller already had. near_clusters must tokenize anyway to build its bag, so it gets the abstract fingerprint for free and hands it back rather than leaving a later pass to re-abstract the same source.
claims.why: near_clusters not in chunk; cannot verify that it calls put_abstract_fp.

observations.what: unit_clusters signature includes memo parameter but body is not shown; implementation may or may not use memo correctly.
CloneMemo._spec method accesses self._spec_by_lang.get(u.language); if u.language is not in dict, returns None; callers must handle None.

exact_fp and abstract_fp use id(u) as key; if u is a temporary and garbage-collected, id could be reused. The docstring claims reference prevents recycling, but only if the memo holds a reference; it does via tuple (u, value).
put_abstract_fp only stores if id not already in cache; no update if already present. This is intentional.
